title: Description of a novel RyR2 mutation in a juvenile patient with symptomatic catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in sleep and during exercise: a case report
case_prompt:
A 17-year-old Caucasian boy was admitted to the ICU after successful out-of-hospital resuscitation. While running, he collapsed; paramedics recorded ventricular fibrillation and restored sinus rhythm with defibrillation. On arrival he was hemodynamically stable (HR 95/min, BP 125/79 mmHg, T 36.5 °C, RR 15/min, SpO2 100% on 4 L nasal cannula). Physical and neurologic examinations were normal.

History revealed multiple prior syncopal episodes during stair climbing, soccer, and once with fright. An exercise ECG had shown multiple premature beats under submaximal stress, and metoprolol succinate 47.5 mg daily was started. He had no other medical history, medications, or family history of sudden death.

Post-arrest resting ECG demonstrated negative T waves in V1 and biphasic T waves in V2. Laboratory tests were normal with no evidence of ischemia or metabolic derangements. Blood gas analysis and chest radiograph were unremarkable. Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal left and right ventricular function without wall motion abnormalities, strain, or valvular disease. Cardiac MRI confirmed the absence of structural abnormalities.

Further diagnostic workup included coronary angiography and electrophysiological testing, but none of those resulted in any relevant finding.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Respiratory or neurovascular causes excluded — “Respiratory disorders (bronchospasm, aspiration) or neurovascular events seemed to be unlikely because the physical examination, blood gas analysis, and a pulmonary x-ray showed normal findings.”  
2. Cardiomyopathies and myocarditis excluded — “we ruled out hypertrophic and dilative cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, and acute myocarditis as potential differential diagnoses.”  
3. Coronary artery disease excluded — “Further diagnostic workup included coronary angiography … but none of those resulted in any relevant finding.”  
4. Electrophysiological substrate for arrhythmia excluded — “electrophysiological testing, but none of those resulted in any relevant finding.”  
5. Other channelopathies excluded by genetic screening — “screening of the patient and family members for other pathogenic mutations (long or short QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome) were also negative.”  
6. CPVT suspected based on history of exercise- and emotion-triggered syncope — “Owing to the patient’s medical history of stress-dependent syncope, we strongly suspected a CPVT as the underlying mechanism for VF.”  
7. CPVT confirmed by genetic testing — “Genetic screening was performed and confirmed the diagnosis of CPVT, revealing a new heterozygous point mutation in the gene for ryanodine receptor type 2, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not been described to date in the literature.”
